servinfo.title: Steering Lower Shaft Removal and Installation

attention4.ptxt: If the steering wheel is turned with the steering lower shaft removed, the neutral setting of the contact coil may be disturbed. If it is turned in either direction more than about two and a half turns, the contact coil will break.
Never turn the steering wheel with the steering lower shaft removed.

s1.ptxt: Turn steering wheel so that vehicle’s front wheels are at straight ahead position.
Make matchmarks (1) on the following parts for correct reinstallation.

item.ptxt: Steering lower shaft joint (2) and steering column (3)
Steering lower shaft joint and pinion shaft (4)

attention3.ptxt: Turn steering wheel a little for removal of steering lower shaft joint bolt.

s1.ptxt: Remove steering column joint bolt (6) and steering lower shaft joint bolt (5).

attention4.ptxt: The steering lower shaft joint bolts are pre-coated with friction stabilizer. If the bolts are reused, they may work loose.
Never reuse the steering lower shaft joint bolts.

s1.ptxt: Check that vehicle’s front wheels are in straight ahead position.
Fit joint part of steering lower shaft (1) onto steering column (2) and pinion shaft (3) while aligning matchmarks (4).

attention3.ptxt: Turn steering wheel a little for installation of steering lower shaft joint bolt (pinion shaft side).

s1.ptxt: Tighten new steering column joint bolt and new steering lower shaft joint bolt to specified torque in numerical order (“1” through “2”) as shown in figure.
